TH5110D1022 has been discontinued by the manufacturer (2026-06). Suggested replacement: TH2320U4006 - FocusPro P200 Programmable, 3H/2C Heat Pump, 2H/2C Conventional, Large Display Thermostat.

The TH5110D1022 is a non-programmable thermostat from Honeywell Home.

A non-programmable thermostat holds one setpoint until someone changes it. That is the whole design, and it is the right design more often than the market admits: in a shop, a rental, a spare room or anywhere occupancy has no schedule, a programmable stat gets overridden permanently within a week and then behaves like this one with extra steps.

Where it hangs decides what it reads. A thermostat measures the air touching it and nothing else, so an interior wall about five feet up, out of direct sun, away from supply registers and doorway drafts, and clear of the back of a wall carrying hot water or flue pipe. Most complaints that a stat is “off by three degrees” are placement, not calibration — the stat is reading the truth about a spot nobody lives in.

These are also the straightforward answer to the C-wire problem. A smart thermostat needs a common wire to power itself continuously, and in an older house that wire is often not in the bundle — which turns a thermostat swap into a wire pull. A non-programmable stat does not draw a continuous 24 V supply for itself, so the wires already on the wall are usually the wires it needs.

If the stat has an adjustable heat anticipator, set it to the current stamped on the primary control rather than leaving it where it arrived. Too low and the burner shuts off early and the room never reaches setpoint
column2:
too high and it overshoots and then coasts cold. It is the one adjustment on a stat like this that changes comfort, and the one most often skipped.

Confirm the system type before ordering — low voltage, line voltage and millivolt thermostats look similar and are not interchangeable.

The YTH6320R1001 is a programmable thermostat from Honeywell Home, supplied as a kit.

7715746545767,"double-pole-line-voltage-programmable-thermostat","UPDATE","

The TL8230A1003 is a line-voltage thermostat from Honeywell Home for electric resistance heat — baseboard, convectors, radiant ceiling or panel heaters.

Line voltage is the distinction that matters here. A low-voltage thermostat switches a 24 V control circuit and lets a furnace or boiler do the work
column2:
a line-voltage thermostat carries the full heater current itself. They are not interchangeable, and a low-voltage stat wired to a baseboard circuit fails immediately.

This is a double-pole thermostat: it breaks both legs of the supply, so the heater is fully de-energized when the thermostat is satisfied or turned off. Double-pole is what most jurisdictions require on 240 V baseboard, and it is what makes the heater safe to work on with the thermostat off.

The programmable schedule lets the heat drop back when the room is empty and recover before it is used again. On electric resistance heat, where every watt is billed at full price, setback is the single largest saving available — there is no efficiency to improve, only run time to remove.

Match the voltage and the pole configuration to the heater circuit, and check the amperage of the heater against the rating of the thermostat. A thermostat sized below the load is the most common cause of a line-voltage stat failing in its first season.
